idea-harness — a local-first AI product-development control plane

Quickstart
the whole loop on the demo provider — no key, about two minutes
  idea init                 create a project + start the daemon
  idea new "<your idea>"    idea → reviewed PRD
  idea next --until-human   design → plan → change set, stops for you
  idea review CHG-1 approve approve the change set
  idea apply CHG-1          write it to your workspace
  idea verify REQ-1 --pass  record evidence
  idea next                 → initiative complete

Commands

Start
  init [<dir>]           initialize a project (defaults to the current directory)
  status [<initiative>]  show initiative + current work
  changed [<initiative>] show What Changed since last look
  doctor                 check daemon/config/state health

Explore & define
  new "<idea>" [--doc <path> …] [--file <path>|-] [--from <initiative>] [--no-wait]
                                             create an initiative and start the workflow; brief from --file/stdin or --doc
  decisions                                  list open/blocked decisions
  questions                                  list open/answered questions
  answer <question> "<answer>" [<initiative>]
                                             answer an open question
  resolve <decision> <option#>|"<resolution>" [<initiative>]
                                             resolve an open decision, by option number or free text
  reopen-decision <decision> [<initiative>]  return a resolved decision to open
  accept-recommendations                     resolve every open decision with its own recommendation
  triage                                     show the ranked "needs your judgment" view
  prd                                        render the reviewed PRD in your terminal
  explain                                    show the Current Understanding
  export [kind]                              export an artifact as markdown
  approve                                    accept the reviewed PRD as it stands
  revise                                     regenerate the PRD from the review findings

Design & plan
  advance [--wait]                           run Design → Execution Plan
  approve-plan                               accept the execution plan as it stands
  revise-plan [--note <text>]                regenerate the execution plan
  plan                                       render the execution plan
  tasks                                      list the ordered plan tasks
  add-task "<title>" --requirement <ref> [--statement <text>] [--priority must|should|could] [--estimate <text>] [--depends-on <ref>] [<initiative>]
                                             add a plan task
  merge-tasks <task1> <task2> [<initiative>] [--yes]
                                             merge two tasks into one
  split-task <task> --title "<title>" --requirements <ref>[,<ref>...] [--statement <text>] [--yes] [<initiative>]
                                             split a task into two or more
  depends-on <task> --on <ref> [--on <ref>...] [<initiative>]
                                             set a task's dependencies
  reorder <task1> <task2> ... [--initiative <ref>]
                                             reorder the plan's tasks
  reopen-phase <architecture|product_design|verification_design> [<initiative>] [--no-wait]
                                             reopen a design phase

Build
  execute [--note <text>] [--wait]           run the next ready task into a change set
  retry [<initiative>] [--model <provider/model>] [--note <text>] [--no-wait]
                                             re-run a failed initiative
  changes                                    list change sets
  change <id>                                show a change set
  apply <id> [--wait]                        apply an approved change set
  revert <id> [--wait]                       roll back a change set
  review <id> <verdict> [--note <text>] [--no-wait]
                                             approve, reject, request changes on, or rerun a change-set review; --accept-findings signs off findings
  executors                                  list executors + capabilities
  executors setup [<kind>]                   wire a coding agent (hermes, omp, acp, or openhands)
  watch                                      watch a run live
  run events <run-id|current> [<initiative>] [--follow] [--json]
                                             print a coding-agent run's events (--follow tails live, --json one object per line)
  runs remote [<initiative>] [--all] [--json]
                                             list the OpenHands executor's remote runs (--all: every initiative)
  steer <run-id|current> "<note>" [<initiative>] [--interrupt]
                                             send a note to a running coding agent (--interrupt ends the turn first)
  cancel <op-id>                             interrupt a running operation

Verify & review
  reviews                                    list review findings
  disposition <finding> <fixed|accepted_risk|not_applicable|duplicate|deferred|rejected|mitigate|not_a_secret> [--note <text>] [<initiative>]
                                             disposition a review finding (not_a_secret also allowlists it)
  pr [<initiative>]                          open a pull request for the initiative's branch (git.branch_per_initiative)
  pr checks <change-set-id>                  show the latest CI status via `gh pr checks`
  verify [<req>]                             run the verification gate; record evidence with --pass/--fail/--waive
  next [--until-human]                       run the next automatable step (--until-human: keep going until a human decision)
  risk                                       show the deterministic risk profile

Understand the graph
  why <type> <id>                            show the provenance chain
  impact <type> <id>                         show dependents + staleness
  trace <type> <id>                          show provenance + dependents
  gaps [<initiative>] [--kind k,...] [--fail-on <sev>] [--all]
                                             list Product Graph gaps, each with the command that closes it (--fail-on: exit 5 at or above a severity)
  assumption <id> accept|dispute|retract     judge an assumption or hypothesis (closes an unvalidated_assumption gap)
  objectives [<initiative>]                  list the initiative's objectives: what each is for, how many requirements serve it, how many metrics measure it
  objective add|edit|link                    add, edit or link an objective (see the rows below)
  objective add "<statement>"                add an objective (never rewritten by a PRD revision)
  objective edit <OBJ>                       edit an objective's statement, rationale, owner, or status
  objective link <REQ> <OBJ>                 record that a requirement serves an objective (--unlink removes it)
  budget [<initiative>] [--set <usd>|--clear]
                                             show spend against the cap, and set or clear it; agent spend that isn't reported isn't counted
  metrics [<initiative>]                     list outcome metrics with their drift: on track, off track, regressed, stale or no data
  metric add|edit|record|measure             add, edit, record or measure an outcome metric (see the rows below)
  metric add <OBJ> "<name>" --target <n>     add a metric to an objective (--target, --direction, source via --command/--url)
  metric edit <MET>                          edit a metric's flags or drop its source
  metric record <MET> <value>                record a measured value and show drift (--note, --at)
  metric measure [<MET>]                     run a metric's command/url source now and record what it reads
  diff                                       structured requirement/decision diff

Configure & connect
  model [--provider <name>] [--all]          show the current model + a curated set (Gemini, OpenAI, …)
  model list [<provider>] [--all]            list providers; a provider (by name or --provider) shows it in full, --all shows every model of every provider
  model ls <provider>                        list a provider's models live (falls back to the catalog offline)
  model set <provider/model>                 set the default model (--role <role> sets one role only)
  model add <name>                           add a provider (--type, --base-url, --key-env)
  key set <provider> [--stdin] | key list    set or list the API keys providers read (set prompts for the key and writes it to .env, never shown)
  key set <provider> [--stdin]               set a provider's API key: prompts (or reads --stdin) and writes it to .env, then reloads the daemon
  key list                                   list each provider's key variable and whether it is set
  env [--json] | env set <NAME> [--stdin]    list the environment variables the plan's tasks need, or set one (prompts and writes it to .env, never shown)
  env set <NAME> [--stdin]                   set an environment variable the plan declared: prints how to obtain it and its URL, prompts (or reads --stdin), and writes it to .env
  integrations [status]                      show Slack/Linear integration health: tokens present, deliveries, socket and poll state
  integrations test slack|linear             post a Slack test message or validate the Linear setup
  config                                     show or validate .idea-harness config
  config validate                            validate .idea-harness/harness.yaml (non-zero exit when invalid)
  docs                                       list uploaded context docs
  docs add <path>                            upload a context doc (--kind, --title)
  ui pair|sessions                           sign a browser on another device in to the web UI, and list or revoke those sessions (see the rows below)
  ui pair [--label <name>] [--qr]            mint a one-time pairing code for a remote browser (--qr draws a QR)
  ui sessions [revoke <id>|--all]            list remote browser sessions; revoke one, or every one
  remote enable|disable|status               turn remote access on or off over Tailscale (enable/disable/status)
  remote enable                              turn remote access on over Tailscale
  remote disable                             turn remote access off: clear the allowed host and stop `tailscale serve`
  remote status                              show the daemon's remote listener and allowed hosts, and whether tailscale serve is up
  capture token|list                         mint a capture token, or list this project's tokens
  capture token [--label <name>]             mint a one-time capture token (present it to POST /api/v1/capture)
  capture list                               list this project's capture tokens (id, label, last used) — never the secret
  channel telegram|slack|email|show          configure a channel (telegram, slack, email) or show the current setup
  channel telegram [--token-env <name>]      turn on Telegram capture; the bot token comes from the named env var (default TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN)
  channel slack --channel <id> [--allowed-users u1,u2] [--bot-token-env n] [--app-token-env n]
                                             turn on Slack (notifications + /idea); a channel ID, not a #name
  channel email --to <a> --from <a> --smtp-host <h> [--smtp-port n] [--smtp-user u] [--smtp-password-env n]
                                             turn on email notifications over SMTP
  channel show                               print the current channel configuration
  mcp [--read-only|--allow-apply] [--dir <path>]
                                             serve this project to MCP clients (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex)

Run & administer
  logs [-f] [n]                              show (or follow) the daemon log
  daemon [--listen <ip:port>] [--tls-cert <file> --tls-key <file>] [--allowed-hosts <h,...>]
                                             run the daemon in the foreground (loopback is always served)
  daemon status|stop                         manage the managed daemon
  dev                                        start the daemon and serve the web UI
  eval [--suite <name|file>] [--model <provider/model>] [--case <name>]
                                             run the eval suite end to end and report per-case results and cost
  version                                    print the version, commit and build state
  help [--format=md]                         show this command list (--format=md emits the docs/cli.md table)

State commands support --json.
